equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.context: The S&P/TSX Composite closed the week to May 14 at 34,268, up 1.2% week-over-week and 31.9% year-over-year. The 12-month advance ranks among the index's widest year-over-year gains since the 2021 commodity recovery, moving in step with a 60.1% year-over-year rise in WTI crude to about US$100.16/bbl as Strait of Hormuz supply disruption lifted the index's energy and materials components19. Gold's 39.1% year-over-year gain to US$4,563.20/oz and copper's 37.3% year-over-year rise to US$6.34/lb reinforced the materials weighting that distinguishes the TSX from the U.S. benchmarks33. The Signal Dispatch cross-reference engine links the energy-led move to 59 oil and gas projects valued at $97.6B in the database. If WTI holds near US$100/bbl, those 59 oil and gas projects would retain the netback support implied by the crude-led March trade surplus, while the database's 7,480 tracked projects, with an aggregate value of $1,472.2B, carry broad exposure to sustained resource pricing at current TSX levels14. The cross-reference engine separately ties the materials strength to 83 manufacturing projects valued at $129.0B, which face the offsetting U.S. steel and aluminum tariff drag noted in the trade data13.

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.context: The S&P 500 ended the week at 7,501, up 2.2% week-over-week and 25.8% year-over-year. The weekly gain came after the Federal Reserve held the fed funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29 for a third consecutive meeting, with markets pricing no Fed changes through the rest of 202623. The 25.8% year-over-year advance marks one of the index's larger 12-month moves since the 2023 disinflation run, recorded as the FOMC cited elevated inflation reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices24.

equities.name: Dow Jones
equities.context: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 50,063, up 0.9% week-over-week and 17.0% year-over-year. The blue-chip benchmark cleared the 50,000 mark following the Fed's hold and amid U.S. growth of 2.0% in Q4 2025 that sustained demand across industrial and healthcare components23. The 17.0% year-over-year gain trailed the broader S&P 500 and Nasdaq, its narrowest relative 12-month performance since the late-2024 industrials rotation24.

equities.name: NASDAQ
equities.context: The Nasdaq Composite closed at 26,635, up 3.2% week-over-week and 38.6% year-over-year. The technology-weighted index posted the largest weekly gain of the four benchmarks after the Fed's third consecutive hold, which markets read as removing near-term tightening risk for rate-sensitive growth shares23. The 38.6% year-over-year advance is the steepest 12-month move among the tracked indices, exceeding the S&P 500's 25.8% over the same window24.
